item.text:
Research round 1 completed for all selected chapters, using the supplied ledger and continuing provisional IDs at E021. No scores or ranking guidance were assigned.

The filesystem is read-only in this worker, so I could not update `research-materials.md` or `research-ledger-manifest.json`. The following is the complete persistence handoff.

### New evidence register entries

- **E021** — *Prayut kickstarts Thailand’s AI mission to boost economy by THB48bn*, The Nation, 9 Dec 2022. Prayut launched an AI mission, directed ministries to build skills and an AI ecosystem, and set 2027 targets for talent, government adoption, infrastructure, regulation, and economic impact. Locator: article lines 8–10, 23–35, 44–55. Maps: `1B.9`, `5B.6`, `8B.1`, `8B.2`, `8B.6`. Official-policy reporting; medium confidence; implementation and outcome evidence absent. [Source](https://www.nationthailand.com/thailand/policies/40022913)

- **E022** — *The Cabinet approved the Thailand National AI Strategy and Action Plan 2022–2027*, NECTEC, 26 Jul 2022. Cabinet approval established a national AI strategy covering infrastructure, skills, regulation, public-sector use, and social/economic goals. Locator: HTML lines 48–80. Maps: `1B.9`, `5B.6`, `8B.1`, `8B.2`, `8B.6`. Official source; high confidence for the policy act, not for delivery or safeguards. [Source](https://www.nectec.or.th/default/en/about/news/cabinet-national-ai-strategy.html)

- **E023** — *Despite Recent Attacks, Southern Thailand’s Peace Talks Are Making Progress*, World Politics Review, 21 Jun 2022. Reports two Kuala Lumpur dialogue rounds, a 40-day Ramadan/Songkran truce, no clashes during the truce period, and later attacks by PULO and BRN. Locator: article title/date and opening conflict-summary section. Maps: `2B.1`, `2B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`, `3B.9`, `3B.10`. Independent analytical reporting; medium confidence; does not establish Prayut’s personal direction of operations. [Source](https://www.worldpoliticsreview.com/in-southern-insurgency-thailand-peace-talks-progress-amid-attacks/)

- **E024** — *At least 349 people, activists, youth monitored, harassed and violated by authorities in 2022*, Thai Lawyers for Human Rights, 29 Dec 2022. Documents at least 349 people monitored or harassed by officials, including home/workplace/school visits, surveillance, photographing, and summonses; 24 were children. TLHR states the total covers reported cases only and may undercount. Locator: HTML lines 35–45. Maps: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `4B.3`, `4B.6`, `4B.9`. Local civil-society documentation; medium confidence; attribution reaches officials, not automatically Prayut. [Source](https://tlhr2014.com/en/archives/52561)

- **E025** — *Thailand: Police Forcibly Disperse APEC Protesters*, Human Rights Watch, 22 Nov 2022. Reports apparently excessive police force, beatings, and rubber-bullet injuries during the 18 Nov APEC protest, and calls for Prayut to order an impartial investigation. Locator: HTML lines 597–610. Maps: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.4`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `4B.3`, `4B.4`, `4B.8`. Rights-monitoring report; medium-high confidence for the documented incident and recommendation; no evidence here that an impartial investigation occurred. [Source](https://www.hrw.org/news/2022/11/22/thailand-police-forcibly-disperse-apec-protesters)

- **E026** — *Thai officials must drop all the ongoing prosecutions under the Emergency Decree*, Amnesty International Thailand, Nov 2022. Amnesty reports at least 1,468 people in 661 protest-related Emergency Decree cases through September 2022, including at least 241 children; it also records acquittals, non-prosecution orders, and convictions. Locator: HTML lines 66–85. Maps: `3B.1`, `3B.4`, `3B.5`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `4B.3`, `4B.4`, `4B.9`. Advocacy/legal analysis; medium confidence; case totals derive from TLHR and are not a judicial finding of unlawful conduct in every case. [Source](https://www.amnesty.or.th/en/news/2022/11/thai-officials-must-drop-all-the-ongoing-prosecutions-under-the-emergency-decree/)

- **E027** — *Thailand: Pegasus spyware found on phones of dissidents involved in mass protests*, Amnesty International, Jul 2022. Reports forensic findings that Pegasus was found on phones of prominent Thai protest organizers and states that the responsible authority was not publicly established; Amnesty called for an independent investigation and legal safeguards. Locator: HTML lines 64–80. Maps: `3B.2`, `3B.5`, `3B.8`, `4B.3`, `4B.6`, `4B.9`. Technical human-rights investigation; medium-high confidence for infection findings, unresolved state attribution. [Source](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2022/07/pegasus-thailand-activists-protests/)

- **E028** — *We Are Reclaiming Our Future*, Amnesty International, Feb 2023, documenting 2020–2022 conduct. The report records child surveillance, home visits, threats, police monitoring, and ineffective domestic protection mechanisms; it includes a specific 2022 case involving a 16-year-old activist followed by police. Locator: PDF pp. 24–26, 37–38, 48; lines 861–901 and 1463–1472. Maps: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.4`, `3B.5`, `3B.7`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `4B.3`, `4B.6`, `4B.9`. Target-period events documented retrospectively; medium-high confidence; not a direct finding against Prayut personally. [PDF](https://www.amnesty.org/en/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/ASA3963362023ENGLISH.pdf)

- **E029** — *Thailand’s Economy Remains Resilient amid Global Headwinds*, World Bank, 14 Dec 2022. Reports Q3 growth of 4.5%, tourism recovery, fiscal measures mitigating household harm, but projected poverty rising from 6.3% in 2021 to 6.6% in 2022. Locator: press-release summary and Thailand Economic Monitor findings. Maps: `5B.1`, `5B.3`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`, `6B.1`, `6B.6`, `6B.10`, `8B.7`. Institutional assessment; high confidence for outcomes and broad policy context; attribution remains shared between government, central bank, and external recovery. [Source](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2022/12/14/thailand-s-economy-remains-resilient-amid-global-headwinds)

- **E030** — *IMF Staff Completes 2022 Article IV Mission to Thailand*, IMF, 13 Jun 2022. Finds recovery supported by policy buffers and accelerated vaccination, but uneven sectoral recovery, 6.1% expected inflation, household-debt risk, and need for targeted vulnerable-group support and productivity investment. Locator: HTML lines 222–240. Maps: `5B.3`, `5B.6`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.6`, `8B.7`, `8B.9`. Independent institutional assessment; high confidence; may overlap the existing E010 and should be merged if the canonical URL/claim key matches. [Source](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2022/06/13/pr22195-imf-staff-completes-2022-article-iv-mission-to-thailand)

- **E031** — *Learning Coin: Open education opportunities for out-of-school migrants, Thailand*, UNESCO, updated 1 Dec 2022. Reports more than 200,000 migrant children estimated out of school, documentation/status barriers, weak multilingual materials, and pandemic-related access problems; describes a UNESCO multilingual digital-library and conditional-cash-transfer intervention. Locator: HTML lines 193–202. Maps: `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.7`, `6B.8`, `6B.10`, `8B.6`. UNESCO program/source; medium-high confidence; much of the baseline evidence predates 2022 and does not establish Prayut’s ownership of the intervention. [Source](https://www.uil.unesco.org/en/litbase/learning-coin-open-education-opportunities-out-school-migrants-thailand)

- **E032** — *Fostering Foundational Skills in Thailand: From a Skills Crisis to a Learning Society*, World Bank/EEF/Thammasat. Reports 64.7% below foundational reading thresholds, 74.1% below digital-skills thresholds, concentration of deficits among rural, northern, and southern populations, and concrete government actions that had not resolved the crisis. Locator: HTML lines 34–50. Maps: `5B.6`, `5B.8`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.5`, `6B.10`, `8B.7`. Independent assessment; high confidence for outcome/distribution context; publication timing is not clearly target-year-specific, so use cautiously. [Source](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/thailand/publication/fostering-foundational-skills-in-thailand)

- **E033** — *DSI searches bid-rigging networks in three provinces*, Department of Special Investigation, 19 Mar 2022. Reports searches in a special case involving alleged e-bidding collusion on post-office construction contracts totaling 67.709 million baht, seizure of financial and procurement records, and continuing investigation. Locator: Thai-language HTML lines 63–78. Maps: `5B.5`, `7B.6`, `8B.5`, `8B.6`. Official investigation record; high confidence that the investigation occurred, but no Prayut/personal-network nexus and no final finding. Retain as context only, not personal-integrity evidence. [Source](https://www.dsi.go.th/en/Detail/20238f629a4994c3a2684abaa5124a7d)

- **E034** — *Constitutional Court Ruling No. 14/2565 (2022)*, Constitutional Court of Thailand. The ruling states that Prayut’s premiership under the 2017 Constitution began on 6 Apr 2017 and therefore had not reached the eight-year limit by 24 Aug 2022. Locator: PDF pp. 1–2, lines 1–47. Maps: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.4`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`, `8B.5`, `8B.9`, `8B.10`. Primary legal record; high confidence for the legal holding; it establishes institutional and succession context, not by itself intent or improper manipulation. [Source](https://www.constitutionalcourt.or.th/occ_en/download/article/article_20231107160628.pdf)

### Chapter yield and unresolved gaps

- **1B:** E021–E022 materially improve target-period dual-use/AI and cyber-policy coverage. The IAEA statement could not be fetched; no ruler-specific nuclear safeguards, proliferation, delivery-system, biological, or crisis-conduct evidence was located. Treaty status and absence of a nuclear arsenal remain country context only. Chapter is bounded but not saturated for ruler attribution.

- **2B:** E023 adds target-period peace-dialogue, truce, attack, and civilian-harm evidence. The blocked Crisis Group document remains discovery-only. No strong evidence was found for Prayut personally initiating cross-border conflict, directing proxies, or accepting/rejecting accountability for civilian harm. The chapter remains open on operational command records and local-language event verification.

- **3B:** E024–E028 materially improve surveillance, protest treatment, emergency-decree prosecution, child protection, police force, and remedy evidence. The evidence is concentrated among Amnesty, HRW, and TLHR, with overlapping underlying protest cases. Prison conditions, broad vulnerable-group protection, independent complaint outcomes, and direct command/knowledge links remain unresolved.

- **4B:** E034 provides a precise primary legal record for the term-limit episode. E025–E028 add protest, surveillance, and civic-space evidence. No 2022 election occurred, so election-observer evidence is inapplicable to the target year; institutional appointments, ECT independence, and digital-control responsibility remain only partly evidenced. Freedom House’s 2022 country page should be reused with additional locators rather than duplicated.

- **5B:** E029–E033 improve macro response, household exposure, education/productivity constraints, and procurement-investigation context. No direct evidence was found tying the DSI procurement case to Prayut personally. Appointments, competition/capture, distribution by region/household, and implementation audits remain gaps.

- **6B:** E029–E032 improve pandemic recovery, household poverty, migrant education access, skill quality, regional inequality, and vulnerable-group context. Direct ruler-attributed service-delivery decisions and affordability/quality evidence remain incomplete; durable institutional effects are unresolved.

- **7B:** The continuation did not recover admissible target-period personal-integrity evidence. E033 is an official procurement investigation without a Prayut nexus; E034 is a legal decision, not an integrity finding. Asset-declaration procedure is documented by the NACC, but Prayut’s actual 2022 declaration, beneficial interests, family benefit, correction, obstruction, and personal response were not retrieved. This remains the principal attribution blocker.

- **8B:** E021–E022 establish explicit AI/cyber program architecture; E023 establishes peace-dialogue execution; E029–E032 establish macro, health, education, and skills implementation/outcome evidence; E034 establishes institutional continuity context. A complete governing portfolio, budgets, appointments, milestones, adaptation, and durability evidence remains unavailable.

### Query and candidate audit

Discovery was varied across:

- broad ruler-period searches;
- event-specific southern peace and Ramadan-truce searches;
- official/source-family searches for IAEA, NECTEC, DSI, NACC, Constitutional Court, IMF, World Bank, UNESCO, Amnesty, HRW, and TLHR;
- adverse searches for surveillance, police force, emergency prosecutions, procurement, and corruption;
- Thai-language searches for cyber policy, procurement, and court records.

Rejected or non-defensible candidates:

- Crisis Group southern-dialogue PDF: HTTP 403; retained as discovery-only, not evidence.
- IAEA Thailand safeguards statement: retrieval error; discovery-only.
- US State Department report through ecoi: cache miss; discovery-only.
- NACC/Prawit luxury-watch material: concerns a deputy prime minister and predates/extends beyond the target period; not attributable to Prayut and excluded from personal-integrity evidence.
- DSI procurement investigation: retained as contextual institutional evidence only; no ruler nexus.
- UNESCO skills report: retained with a temporal-fit caution because the target-year publication timing is unclear.

### Cross-chapter reuse and same-source splits

- Amnesty’s child-protester report supports both 3B and 4B, but its claims should remain separate from the shorter Amnesty UK summary.
- HRW’s APEC protest report supports 3B and 4B; it is a single incident, not two independent events.
- TLHR’s 2022 monitoring count supports 3B and 4B but explicitly covers reported cases only.
- NECTEC and The Nation concern the same AI-policy theme but are different source families; NECTEC is the primary policy record, while The Nation supplies Prayut’s launch and implementation framing.
- IMF and World Bank provide distinct institutional assessments, though E030 should be merged with E010 if the earlier ledger used the same IMF URL and materially identical claim.
- Freedom House 2022 should be locator-split and reused rather than duplicated.
- E034 is a distinct primary legal source and should not replace the earlier Reuters account; the two establish the legal holding and external interpretation separately.

### Local-data audit

The supplied local facts were retained as follows:

- **1B:** treaty/inventory and non-nuclear exposure context only; no local fact establishes Prayut’s conduct.
- **2B:** LF073–LF076 and LF149–LF152 retained for 2022 conflict exposure and military-burden context; not evidence of initiation, proportionality, or peace responsibility.
- **3B:** LF322–LF331, LF440–LF445 and related longitudinal facts retained as national physical-integrity, repression, violence, and civil-liberties context; not automatically attributed.
- **4B:** LF616–LF623, LF884–LF898 and related regime/constraint facts retained as institutional context; E034 supplies the target-period legal record.
- **5B:** LF1019–LF1025 and LF1246–LF1251 retained for macro, distribution, and productivity context; outcomes do not establish ruler competence without policy linkage.
- **6B:** LF1325–LF1334 retained for welfare/service context; no local row independently establishes implementation, equity, or durability.
- **7B:** LF1407–LF1410 retained only as country-level integrity/governance context; they cannot satisfy the personal-nexus requirement.
- **8B:** LF1447–LF1448 and related capacity facts retained as inherited implementation context; they do not identify Prayut’s program or adaptation.

No supplied `error_methodology_ids` were present. No local fact was treated as proof of peacefulness, safety, personal integrity, or ruler effectiveness.
